source.paperTitle: Data-driven prediction of possible quality deterioration in injection molding processes
source.dataAvailability: The publisher states that the data used in the study are confidential.

paperBackedExperimentContext.process: real production injection moulding of bottle caps
processEvidence: online process-data streams from regular production

ownershipBoundary.requiredAuthority: the industrial data owner or a person/organisation explicitly authorised by that owner to approve research access and automated aggregate profiling

primary.name: Kurt Pichler
primary.role: surviving paper co-author and current LCM researcher
primary.purpose: identify the confidential-data owner and route an authorization request to the person with authority to approve research use

organisationalFallback.purpose: route the request if the direct author address changes or if owner approval must be handled institutionally

currentContactRoute.historicalAuthorBoundary: Edwin Lughofer died in 2023; outreach must not depend on his former contact address.

acceptableAuthorizationPaths.description: The industrial data owner, or an explicitly authorised representative, approves a controlled research transfer to MouldMaster for aggregate profiling.
minimumTerms: purpose is limited to injection-moulding research/benchmark profiling
raw rows and traces will not be committed to the repository or published
only aggregate schemas, counts, fingerprints and non-identifying diagnostics may be retained
storage, retention, deletion and confidentiality requirements are documented
any company, machine, product or operator identifiers are removed or handled under the owner's rules

acceptableAuthorizationPaths.description: The data remain inside LCM/the industrial owner's environment; the owner or LCM runs an agreed MouldMaster profiler and returns only an aggregate result artifact.
minimumTerms: the exact profiler version or commit is recorded
the profiler emits no raw rows, traces or sensitive identifiers
source file fingerprints or owner-approved stable identifiers are included where permitted
measurement semantics and units are supplied sufficiently to distinguish measured signals from setpoints, labels and derived fields
the owner approves publication of the resulting aggregate counts/metadata

requiredAuthorizationEvidence: Written permission is captured from the owner or an explicitly authorised representative.
The permission explicitly covers automated aggregate profiling or owner-side execution of the profiler.
The permission states whether aggregate schemas, counts, fingerprints and non-identifying diagnostics may be retained and published.
Any NDA, data-processing, storage, retention, deletion, geographic or attribution restrictions are recorded before execution.
The delivered or owner-side-profiled data are linked unambiguously to the 7,162-cycle experiment reported in DOI 10.1016/j.asoc.2023.111029.
profilingGateAfterAuthorization: Fingerprint the exact delivered files or record owner-approved stable source identifiers.
Reconcile the delivered cycle count to the paper-reported horizon of 7,162 production cycles without assuming one row equals one cycle.
Establish signal names, units, sampling/time bases and cycle grouping from source documentation or the delivered schema.
Separate directly measured process/quality values from commands, setpoints, identifiers, transformed trends, model outputs and labels.
Confirm how the three optical quality criteria align to production cycles and whether they are raw measurements or derived inspection features.
Count only delivered measured values whose semantics and ordering are established.
Emit aggregate outputs only and retain no raw confidential production rows or arrays in the repository or CI artifacts.

decision.nextAction: Contact Kurt Pichler/LCM to identify the industrial data owner and request either controlled-transfer authorization or owner-side execution approval.

evidenceBoundary: The paper is strong Tier-B evidence of a real 7,162-cycle bottle-cap production campaign with three optically measured quality criteria and naturally occurring process/material changes. However, the publisher explicitly states that the data used are confidential, and no public dataset-specific reuse licence or named industrial data owner was located. The open-access status of the article does not license the underlying production data. Therefore the source remains non-executable and contributes zero accepted measured samples unless the actual owner, or an explicitly authorised representative, approves a controlled profiling path.
